name: Release approvals: one answer everywhere
summary: I drove release approvals through the real desk controls on Ashworth (probate, two personal representatives), Hale (living, with a shotgun) and a trust estate with a co-trustee. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/REL (sN.js, out/sN.out, saved papers in out/). The common path works and agrees with itself. A partial approval, a co-representative added after an approval and a line with no taker all read the same on the Releases bar, the card, the rows, the request and the sign-out offers, and the estate's staff refusal holds at the write. The weakness is underneath: an approval is a name stuck to a line, not to what was approved. Once recorded, it survives any change to where the line goes, who takes it and what it is worth. A request already confirmed as sent is never checked against the line again. A name typed into the Authorized By box counts as written approval. So an executor's signature for "Auction, Kodner Galleries, $2,400" lets the painting be signed out on the iPad to a cousin at $24,000. The sign-out sheet, the pickup list and the Disposition Ledger then print "Approved in writing by Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12)" against a destination no fiduciary ever saw. A discerning trust attorney who compares the signed copy in Drive with the ledger finds them disagreeing. Several states contradict each other. A clock can be signed for by the beneficiary while it is recorded as with the appraiser. Havellin's own receipt prints a revolver "delivered to me by Havellin", against the firearms rule. The custody dialog records a firearm as released to a relative with one press and no flag. The ledger and the close question are silent about lines that left without every fiduciary's signature. For the concierge, the record step is only about eight presses whatever the line count, which is good. But the desk cannot filter by approval state, the iPad sign-out buttons are 21 px tall, and the dashboard card hides the out-of-date-draft warning the desk shows. Fix first: tie each approval to what it approved (destination, recipient, value band), and check a sent request against the paper when it is recorded.
works_well: A partial approval is recorded and said the same way everywhere. After Thomas alone signed, the bar read '3 on the request still unsigned', the rows 'approval incomplete', the card 'Nora Ashworth has not approved it' and the sign-out rows 'awaiting written approval', and the dialog's note said so before saving (s1 E).

A co-representative recorded after an approval reopens every earlier approval. Lines already picked up turn to 'ratification owed' on the rows, the bar, the card and the request's 'Already released: for ratification' section, and the Kodner sign-out is withdrawn (s3 D2).
On an estate the staff rule refuses at the write and names the person. 'Ashley Jerome', 'ashley  jerome' and 'Anthony Graziano Jr' as buyer were all refused with nothing changed (s2 B, B2, B4).
The sign-out dialog lists a line still waiting for approval as disabled ('awaiting written approval: not offered'), so the glass route cannot release an unapproved estate line (s1, s9).
While a draft is waiting, the desk card and the bar both flag a line changed after the draft was made, and offer Discard draft and I've sent it (s5 A).
A line with nobody named to take it is held off the request and named on the card and the bar ('Hold them off').

Living narrowing works. Only the shotgun and the line going to a Havellin person needed written approval, the living request carried exactly those two, and the staff caution printed above the table the client initials (s4 C).

The request reads as a letter. The firearms block names a missing serial or dealer as 'not covered for transport', and the trust version uses co-trustee, Successor Trustee and 'the trust's records' throughout (s4 C, s13).
No horizontal overflow at 1024 or 390 px. The Record approval and sign-out dialogs fit with Save on screen (s11).
measurements: Presses on the desk to send a 3-line request and record its signed copy: open the Releases bar 1, Send request 1, I've sent it 1, Record the signed request 1, two fiduciary ticks 2, Record approval 1, File the signed request 1 plus the file picker. That is 8 presses whatever the line count (s1.js; sending from Gmail is outside the app).
Sign-out per taker: Sign out N to … 1, the signature, Sign and file 1. That is 2 presses plus the signature (s3.js D, s6.js B/C).

Button heights on the Releases card at 1024 px (iPad landscape): Sign out 2 to Kodner Galleries 219×21 px, Sign out 1 to Carla Mendes 194×21 px, Void 40×15 px. At 390 px the same buttons are 38 px tall (s11.js, getBoundingClientRect).
Horizontal overflow of the desk with the Releases bar open: 0 px at 1024 and 0 px at 390 (s11.js).
Record approval dialog at 390×844: 585 px tall, its Save button's bottom edge at y=822 (s11.js).
After approval, one press re-routes an approved estate line, and 0 confirms or flags appear (s2.js A: s.dialogs stayed empty after changing the disposition, the recipient and the value of e01).
Lines whose recipient or value changed after a request was confirmed as sent: flagged in 0 places. Checked the bar, the card and the Record dialog (s1.js D/E).
verifier_note: The REL report is trustworthy. I reproduced every behavioural claim myself, in seven scripts of my own under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/REL-verify (v1.js to v7.js, outputs in out/v1.out to out/v7.out, papers saved beside them). Each one drives the real controls on step 99's Ashworth and Hale seeds, and every check matched the auditor's account. Fixtures were reachable states. The only seeded approvals are authBy and approvalDate, which is exactly what invSaveApproval writes. James was added through jobListPut, the writer Edit Client's save uses. The extra firearm, Junk and FFL lines are ordinary lines with approvals recorded. Corrections: I rated REL-02 high rather than fix-now. REL-05 goes down to medium, because the bar already flags 'signed approval not filed to Drive', and REL-17 and REL-28 go down to low. REL-20 conflicts with the Domain rule that defines 'released to a person'. REL-22's Junk half conflicts with 'Donations and removals are outside it'. Part of REL-27 is the KNOWN singular/plural bug. REL-09's behaviour is confirmed, but its proposal is aimed at the weaker case. A distribution to a co-representative who is also a beneficiary is ordinary on family estates, so a caution there would mostly be noise. The real gap is that a Sell to a co-representative (Nora Ashworth as buyer) is accepted with no caution at all, the self-dealing case of §733.610. REL-10, REL-21, REL-24 and REL-26 rest on code read plus dialog text, not on a paper outcome. Nothing was refuted.

findings.title: An approval stays recorded after the line's destination, recipient or value changes, and the papers then claim it
findings.where: Releases card › Leaving the property; row disposition and Who takes it boxes; sign-out dialog; Vendor Pickup List; Disposition Ledger. invApprovalComplete (havellin.html:31383) reads authBy/approvalDate only; _invEdit (29700-29790) never touches authBy on a disposition, channel or fmv edit; signoutGroups (31648); signoutSheetHtml (31693) prints invApprovalSignedText; dispositionLedger (34374).
findings.evidence: REL/s2.js (out/s2.out) A: e01 was approved by both PRs on Oct 12 for Auction · Kodner Galleries at $2,400. I changed it on the row to Distribute · 'Cousin Pete Ashworth' at $24,000 with no dialog. invApprovalComplete stayed true, and the card offered 'Sign out 1 to Cousin Pete Ashworth'. Its dialog said 'Only lines every co-representative has approved in writing are offered' and listed the painting. REL/s9.js (out/s9-pickup-sheet.html, out/s9-ledger.html): e02, approved for Kodner, was retyped to Palm Beach Estate Buyers at $600 and signed out. The sheet that vendor signed prints 'Approved in writing by Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)'. The ledger prints 'Auction · Palm Beach Estate Buyers · Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)', while the Oct 12 signed copy in Drive says Kodner. The same gap holds when Agent Two renames or re-values an unreviewed approved line (reasoning from _avRename/agentValueAfterCloseUp: neither reads approval).
findings.tc_impact: The concierge gets no warning that a re-route needs a fresh signature, so a routine change, or an Agent Two re-value, quietly turns an old signature into authority for a new destination. The trust attorney finds the ledger and the vendor's sheet claiming written approval for a sale or gift the fiduciaries never saw, and the signed paper in Drive contradicts them. That is a breach of the 'every fiduciary approves every release' rule on the record itself.
findings.proposal: Tie each approval to what it approved. When _invEdit or _invBulkApply changes the disposition or channel of a line whose approval is recorded, or moves its fmv across INV_LINE_INITIAL_MIN, show one confirm before writing: 'Approved Oct 12 by Thomas and Nora for Auction · Kodner Galleries. Changing this means that approval no longer covers it: it goes on the next request.' OK clears authBy/approvalDate through the existing sticky-clear stamp (clearedAt), so the line becomes fresh or, if it has already gone, ratification owed. Cancel puts the box back. For the agents, _avWrite and _avRename skip or flag a line with a recorded approval. No new item field: the decision lives in the existing two fields plus clearedAt. The sign-out sheet and the ledger then only ever print approvals the paper supports.
findings.vnote: Through the row's own controls I moved e01 (approved by both for Auction · Kodner, $2,400) to Distribute · Cousin Pete Ashworth at $24,000, and e02 to Palm Beach Estate Buyers at $600. Not one dialog appeared, and both lines stayed invApprovalComplete=true. The card offered 'Sign out 1 to Cousin Pete Ashworth', and its dialog said 'Only lines every co-representative has approved in writing are offered' with the painting listed. I signed e02 out on the glass. The filed sheet's column 'Approved in writing by' reads 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)' for a buyer the Oct 12 signed copy never named. The ledger prints 'Distribute · Cousin Pete Ashworth · Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)'. In code, _invEdit (29700-29860) never touches authBy or approvalDate on a disposition, channel or fmv edit, and invApprovalComplete (31383) reads only those two fields. This is a false written-authority claim on a paper. The Agent Two half is reasoning only.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v1.js → out/v1.out (A: dialogs [] and state complete:true; B: sheet; C: cousin's dialog; D: ledger rows), out/v1-pickup-sheet.html, out/v1-ledger.html; havellin.html:29700-29860, 31383

findings.title: A line changed after the request was confirmed as sent is recorded as approved, with no check against the paper
findings.where: Releases card › Approval request › Record the signed request; Releases bar. approvalRequestChanged (32647) returns [] unless docDraftPending(st); invRecordApproval (33094) lists the lines as they are now; approvalRequestSig (32633).
findings.evidence: REL/s1.js (out/s1.out, out/s1-request.html): the request went out and I've sent it was pressed. The paper reads '#4 … Goodwill Palm Beach (Donate) … Initial once … each under $500' and '#10 Walnut dresser $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers … Initial once … under $500'. I then typed e10's Total to $2,900 and e04's recipient to Habitat ReStore. The bar (D) still read '3 on the request still unsigned' and the card said nothing. The Record dialog (E) listed '#4 … Donate · Habitat ReStore'. Recording both signatures (F) left e04 approved for Habitat ReStore and e10 approved at $2,900 with no initial of its own, and 'Sign out 1 to Habitat ReStore' was offered. The card's own advice while the draft waited, 'Already sent? Tap I'ves sent it', is what makes the warning vanish.
findings.tc_impact: The concierge records a signed copy against lines that no longer match it, without being told. The fiduciary initialled '$450, to Goodwill', and the record says they approved '$2,900, to Habitat'.
findings.proposal: Keep the fingerprint check after the send: in approvalRequestChanged, drop the docDraftPending guard for the sent request and compare against updatedAt > sentAt. Show it on the card and the bar ('2 lines changed since this request went: record them only if the signed copy shows the new terms'). In invRecordApproval, list each changed line unticked by default with '⚠ changed since the request was sent'. A flag and a default, never a refusal. This needs no new field (req.sig is already stored).
findings.vnote: I sent the request, then changed e10 to $2,900 while the draft waited. The desk card flagged it. I then pressed the dashboard's I've sent it. From that moment approvalRequestChanged returns [] (its docDraftPending guard, 32647), and the card shows no warning. Re-routing e04 to Habitat ReStore after the send drew no flag on the bar or the card. Record the signed request listed '#4 … Donate · Habitat ReStore'. Recording Thomas and Nora left e04, e07 and e10 approved at their new terms; e10 is now $2,900, and the paper gave it no initial box of its own. I rated it high rather than fix-now because the person recording sees the new terms in the dialog. REL-01's fix would not cover it, since these lines had no approval when they changed.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v2.js → out/v2.out (A, B, C: 'approvalRequestChanged now: []'; D/E dialog; F refs), out/v2-request.html; havellin.html:32647-32666

findings.title: Havellin's beneficiary receipt prints a firearm as 'delivered to me by Havellin'
findings.where: Releases card › Leaving the property › Margaret's row: Print receipt / File signed receipt. invReceiptGroups (31994) groups a Distribute firearm under the person until a dealer route exists (invViaDealer); invReceiptHtml (33372); printBeneficiaryReceipt (33409).
findings.evidence: REL/s6.js and REL/s7.js (out/s7.out, out/s7-receipt.html): an approved 'Colt revolver' (Firearms, Distribute to Margaret Ashworth, no serial, no dealer route) shows on Margaret's row as 'release to a person · 2 lines (#7, #41) … Print receipt … File signed receipt (#7, #41)'. The printed receipt lists '41 Colt revolver' under 'I acknowledge that I received the property listed above … delivered to me by Havellin Palm Beach, LLC'. The glass sign-out for the same row leaves the firearm off (signoutLineKind returns '' for a firearm), so the paper route and the glass route disagree.
findings.tc_impact: The concierge is handed a printed paper in which a beneficiary signs that Havellin gave her a handgun. The firearms protocol says Havellin never hands a firearm to anyone; the dealer does the transfer. Counsel would treat it as a protocol and liability failure on a signed document.
findings.proposal: Leave firearms out of invReceiptGroups' person groups whatever the dealer route, using the same test signoutLineKind uses. On the row, a firearm Distribute line with no dealer route reads 'firearm: record the dealer route; the dealer's receipt is filed, never ours'. invReceiptOwed returns false for a firearm with no dealer route, so the bar's 'signed receipts owed' stops counting it.
findings.vnote: I added an approved Colt revolver (Firearms, Distribute to Margaret Ashworth, no dealer route) beside the approved clock. Margaret's row read 'release to a person · 2 lines (#7, #41) · no signed receipt filed for #7, #41 · Print receipt'. Pressing Print receipt produced a receipt that lists '41 Colt revolver' under 'I acknowledge that I received the property listed above … delivered to me by Havellin Palm Beach, LLC as directed in writing by Thomas A…'. The glass dialog for the same taker listed only #7. invReceiptGroups (31994) leaves a firearm out only once invViaDealer holds, though the code's own comment says Havellin never hands one to anyone. That makes the signed paper's legal wording wrong.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v3.js → out/v3.out (A rows and kinds, B: 'receipt lists Colt: true'), out/v3-receipt.html; havellin.html:31994-32030, 33372-33420

findings.title: The Chain of custody dialog records a held firearm as 'Released' to a relative with one press and no flag
findings.where: Line record › Chain of custody dialog. addCustodyEvent (30484): no invTransportBlocked, invReleaseBlocked or approval check; 'Released' is the default action. The event then makes invRecordedGone true (31924).
findings.evidence: REL/s12.js (out/s12.out): g1 is a shotgun, row chip '⚠ held no dealer route', with no approval recorded. I opened Chain of custody, typed 'Uncle Bob Ashworth' with a date and pressed Add event. No dialog appeared, and the list read 'Released · Uncle Bob Ashworth · Oct 25, 2026'. Afterwards the row read 'held · ratification owed · no signed receipt' (the receipt is owed from Margaret, the channel). The bar read '1 for ratification · 1 signed receipt owed', so the next request will ask the fiduciaries to ratify a firearm handed to a relative.
findings.tc_impact: One mis-chosen default writes a record of exactly what the protocol forbids. The app then treats it as routine paperwork (a ratification, a receipt) rather than an incident. A reader of the custody log or the package sees a firearm released to family with Havellin's stamp on it.
findings.proposal: In addCustodyEvent, ask the same rules the sign-out asks before writing a Released or Transferred event on an estate line. For a firearm: run invTransportBlocked and show 'A firearm moves only to a licensed dealer, by Anthony, on written authority: record it as an incident instead?' (Open Incidents), keeping the event only on a second, explicit choice. For an unapproved estate line: one sentence naming the missing signers and that it will be listed for ratification. Default the action select to an empty 'Choose…' rather than Released.
findings.vnote: I opened Chain of custody on an unapproved estate shotgun (row chip '⚠ held no dealer route'). The default action is Released. I typed 'Uncle Bob Ashworth' and a date and pressed Add event: no dialog, and the list read 'Released · Uncle Bob Ashworth · Oct 25, 2026 · recorded by Ashley Jerome'. The row then read 'held no dealer route ratification owed no signed receipt', and the bar read '1 for ratification · 1 signed receipt owed'. addCustodyEvent (30484) asks no gate at all, neither firearm nor approval.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v4.js → out/v4.out (A, A2); havellin.html:2815 (select, Released first), 30484-30505

findings.title: A name typed into Authorized By counts as written approval: the sign-out opens with no signed paper, and the playbook says to do it
findings.where: Line record › Disposition › Authorized By / Approval Date boxes (_invEdit authBy branch, 29746); the bulk bar's Record approval on living work prefills 'Signed by' with the client's name (invRecordApproval, 33094); the playbook's symptom table (concierge-guide.html:1073, CONCIERGE_GUIDE.md:1063).
findings.evidence: REL/s3.js (out/s3.out) C2: I typed 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth' and 2026-10-25 into e04's record. invApprovalComplete returned true at once, the card offered 'Sign out 1 to Goodwill Palm Beach', and the only trace was the bar's amber '1 signed approval not filed to Drive'. REL/s4.js D on Hale: Record approval on the shotgun opened with 'Signed by' already set to 'Robert Hale', and one press recorded written approval of a firearm with nothing in hand. The playbook row 'No written authority on file' tells the concierge to 'Record Authorized By and Approval Date in the item panel'.
findings.tc_impact: The rule that verbal approval never counts ('so a refusal, not a flag' at the sign-out) can be met by typing two names. Nothing tells the attorney later whether an approval came from a signed paper or a keystroke.
findings.proposal: Make the dialog the only way to record an approval and the box read-only: show who signed and when, with a 'Correct…' link that asks for a reason and stamps authBySetAt. In the sign-out dialog, mark a line whose approval has no filed signed copy covering it: '⚠ approval recorded, signed copy not filed: file it first or sign out anyway'. A flag with the way forward, keeping 'flag, never block' for the paper. Leave the living 'Signed by' blank. Restate the playbook row and the manual to 'Record the signed request, then File the signed request'.
findings.vnote: In e04's record I typed 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth' and 2026-10-25. invApprovalComplete returned true at once, and the card offered 'Sign out 1 to Goodwill Palm Beach'. The only trace is the bar's 'signed approvals not filed to Drive'. On Hale, Record approval for the shotgun opened with 'Signed by' set to 'Robert Hale' (code: invRecordApproval prefills job.name on living work). The playbook row 'No written authority on file' (concierge-guide.html:1073, CONCIERGE_GUIDE.md:1063) and the manual (manual.html:2523) say to type Authorized By and Approval Date. I lowered it to medium: the bar does flag an approval with no signed copy filed, and the typed box is a person's attestation. It conflicts with no decided rule.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v5.js → out/v5.out (C: complete true, sign-out offered; E: signer value 'Robert Hale'); concierge-guide.html:1073

findings.title: An item recorded as with the appraiser can be signed out to a beneficiary; it then reads as both gone and still out
findings.where: Releases card › Leaving the property: Carla Mendes' row and Margaret Ashworth's row. signoutGroups (31648) puts a line in its leaving group and its appraisal group independently; invOutForAppraisal is not read by the leaving kinds.
findings.evidence: REL/s6.js (out/s6.out): e07 (grandfather clock, bequest to Margaret, linked to Carla Mendes, approved). B: I signed the hand-off to Carla on the glass, and the row read '⚖ with Carla Mendes since Oct 26, 2026'. C: 'Sign out 1 to Margaret Ashworth' was still offered with the clock ticked. Margaret signed and the receipt was filed. Afterwards e07 had out=true, gone=true and receipt=true, the row still read 'with Carla Mendes', and Carla's row still offered 'Check 1 back in from Carla Mendes'. The reverse order is offered too (s1 F: both 'Sign out 1 to Margaret' and 'Sign out 1 to Carla' at once).
findings.tc_impact: A beneficiary signs that she received a clock sitting in an appraiser's office, and the close-out (closeOpenWorkFlag 'still out with an appraiser') contradicts the signed receipt. Exactly the kind of chain-of-custody inconsistency a trust officer catches.
findings.proposal: In signoutGroups, put a line that invOutForAppraisal answers in its leaving group's `waiting` with the reason 'with Carla Mendes for appraisal: check it back in first', and the dialog lists it disabled with that reason. Leave a line already recorded gone (invRecordedGone) out of the appraisal hand-off group. One rule each way, read by the card and the dialog.
findings.vnote: With the clock approved, I signed its hand-off to Carla on the glass. The row read '⚖ with Carla Mendes since Oct 26, 2026', yet 'Sign out 1 to Margaret Ashworth' was still offered with e07 ticked. I signed that too. Afterwards e07 reads {out:true, gone:true, receipt:true}. Carla's row offers 'Check 1 back in from Carla Mendes', and closeOpenWorkFlag says '#7 with Carla Mendes', against Margaret's filed receipt. signoutGroups (31648) puts the line in each group independently.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v3.js → out/v3.out (C: Margaret dialog ticked e07:true; e07 state; Carla row; close question)

findings.title: The bulk bar's request and Record approval on an estate take Keep and already-approved lines, and a Keep approval later authorises a Junk run
findings.where: Bulk bar › Approval request / Send request / Record approval. invWrittenReleasePicked (31239) returns the selection unfiltered when invFiduciaryMode; printApprovalRequest(…, true) (32310) prints it; _renderInvBulk offers the three on every estate selection.
findings.evidence: REL/s5.js (out/s5.out, out/s5-bulk-request.html) C: I picked #18 Stand mixer (Keep), #1 (already approved) and #4. The bulk request printed '18 Stand mixer … Keep … Initial once for the item above marked Keep, with no recipient named yet', with #1 asked again. Record approval saved 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth' on the Keep line. D: I set #18 to Junk with Haul-It. The bar then counted it as approved and ready ('3 ready to sign out'), and no new signature was ever asked for the haul-away.
findings.tc_impact: A sweep picked for another reason, such as a room, sends the fiduciaries a confusing paper ('approve a Keep') and writes approvals onto lines that are not leaving. Those approvals turn into release authority later.
findings.proposal: In invWrittenReleasePicked, apply invWrittenReleaseNeeded and drop already-complete lines on an estate as it does on living work. The bulk confirm names what it left out ('2 of 5 selected are not leaving or are already approved'), and the three buttons appear only when a picked line needs approval. Together with REL-01, a disposition change after any recorded approval asks first.
findings.vnote: On an estate I picked #18 (Keep), #1 (already approved) and #4. invWrittenReleasePicked returned all three, since it returns the selection unfiltered in fiduciary mode (31239). The bulk paper prints '18 Stand mixer … Keep · Initial once for the item above marked Keep, with no recipient named yet', which also goes against the 'Hold them off' rule, and it re-asks #1. Record approval wrote 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth' onto the Keep line. Setting #18 to Junk · Haul-It then left it approval-complete, with nothing asked.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v5.js → out/v5.out (A); REL-verify/v6.js → out/v6-bulk-request.html; havellin.html:31239-31242

findings.title: The Disposition Ledger and the close question say nothing about lines that left without every fiduciary's approval
findings.where: Closing bar › Disposition Ledger card; Close job's confirm. dispositionLedger (34374) gaps: undecided, noRecipient, pending, recon only; closeOpenWorkFlag (24595) names rooms, recipients and appraiser hand-offs only.
findings.evidence: REL/s10.js (out/s10.out, out/s10-ledger.html): e10 left on Oct 20 with no approval, and e04 left on Oct 22 with Thomas alone signed out of two. The ledger's gap list names undecided lines, pending proceeds and lines on no statement, but neither of these. Its rows read '#4 … Authorized by Thomas Ashworth (Oct 21, 2026)', with nothing marking that Nora never signed, and '#10 … Authorized by —'. Code read: the close confirm built in applyJobTransition from _ledg plus closeOpenWorkFlag carries no approval or ratification sentence (I could not reach the dialog itself in s10, because Close job was refused for unrated vendors).
findings.tc_impact: The paper the representative signs to close the estate looks complete while it holds releases without written authority. The attorney has to cross-check every Authorized-by cell against the fiduciary list by hand, the twenty-year-appraiser-with-a-spreadsheet work the desk is meant to beat.
findings.proposal: Add two gaps to dispositionLedger and its head: 'N lines left before every fiduciary approved them: #10, #4 (ratification owed)' and 'N leaving lines have no complete written approval'. Both read invRatificationOwed and _approvalLineOpen, the existing rules. Print 'incomplete: still to sign Nora Ashworth' in the Authorized-by cell where invApprovalGap answers, and add the same two sentences to closeOpenWorkFlag. Flags, never refusals.
findings.vnote: Through the record boxes, e04 got Thomas alone, then a Date of Disposition, and e10 got a Date of Disposition with no approval. Both are invRatificationOwed=true. The ledger's gap block names only undecided lines, pending proceeds and the statements. Its #4 row reads 'Authorized by Thomas Ashworth (Oct 21, 2026)' with no mark that Nora never signed. The page text has no ratification or approval-gap wording anywhere. closeOpenWorkFlag returned only the rooms sentence. Code confirms it: dispositionLedger (34374) and closeOpenWorkFlag (24595) read no approval rule.
findings.vrepro: REL-verify/v7.js → out/v7.out, out/v7-ledger.html; havellin.html:24595-24611, 34374-34395, 34480-34500

findings.title: A co-trustee or co-representative receiving an item approves their own distribution, and no caution says so
findings.where: Release Approval Request; INV_RELEASE_CAUTIONS (32111); invReleaseCautions (32241).
findings.evidence: REL/s13.js (out/s13.out, out/s13-trust-request.txt): on a trust estate where Ruth Price is Co-Trustee, '#3 Dining chairs … Distribute · Ruth Price' prints with only a group initial and no caution. Ruth is one of the two 'Approved by' signature lines.
findings.tc_impact: A trustee approving a distribution to themself is a self-dealing question every trust officer and attorney looks for. The request lets it pass as an everyday group initial, so the reader must spot it unaided.
findings.proposal: Add a caution `fiduciaryRecipient` (estate only): its test is that invRecipientName(channel) matches a jobFiduciaries entry (samePerson). Badge 'GOING TO RUTH PRICE, A CO-TRUSTEE SIGNING THIS REQUEST', with its own initial (invOwnInitial already gives a caution its own box) and a short body: 'a fiduciary receiving property from the trust or estate: confirm it with counsel and the other fiduciaries before initialling'. An agent call (the room check's pattern, strict tool) gets the request's own HTML and the photograph, and answers which signature lines are signed, which initial boxes and group rows are initialled and which lines are struck, each with its confidence. The dialog opens pre-ticked from that answer, with anything uncertain unticked and marked; the concierge confirms and presses Record. The agent flags, a person records, and the photograph is the filed copy. The DocuSign route Anthony has already chosen to build next makes this automatic for anything sent; this covers paper handed over in person.
